_meta.description: Documented screen reader bugs and quirks sourced from ARIA-AT test results and a11ysupport.io. Each bug is tied to a role or property, a specific SR, and optionally a browser.

bugs.description: VoiceOver on Chrome does not announce the 'alert' role for dynamically added alerts. Content is read but without the assertive interruption behavior.
bugs.workaround: Use Safari for VoiceOver testing, or add role='alert' to a container that exists in the DOM before content is injected.

bugs.description: JAWS does not read aria-describedby content in virtual cursor mode by default. Users must press Insert+F1 to hear the description.
bugs.workaround: Ensure critical information is in the accessible name (aria-label/aria-labelledby), not just the description.

bugs.description: NVDA with Firefox sometimes does not announce the expanded/collapsed state change when a combobox is toggled.
bugs.workaround: Ensure aria-expanded is toggled on the combobox element itself, not a child.

bugs.description: VoiceOver on Safari does not recognize elements with role='table' as tables unless they also have a caption or aria-label. Without a name, the table structure is flattened.
bugs.workaround: Always provide an accessible name for ARIA tables via aria-label or aria-labelledby.

bugs.description: JAWS 2023 and earlier do not announce aria-current='step' or aria-current='location'. Only 'page' and 'true' values are reliably announced.
bugs.workaround: Use aria-current='page' when possible, or provide visual indicators alongside aria-current.

bugs.description: Orca does not automatically announce alert role live regions. No automatic announcement is triggered when content changes.
bugs.workaround: No reliable workaround. Consider alternative notification mechanisms for Orca users.

bugs.description: VoiceOver announces expanded/collapsed state but uses inconsistent wording. Sometimes says 'expanded' and other times 'open' depending on the role of the element.
bugs.workaround: None needed — the state is still conveyed, just with different wording.

bugs.description: NVDA does not announce aria-required on custom controls (div[role='textbox']) in Chrome. Works correctly on native input elements.
bugs.workaround: Use native HTML form elements where possible. If using custom controls, add 'required' to the visible label text.

bugs.description: JAWS does not recognize role='meter'. The element is read as plain text without the meter value context.
bugs.workaround: Use the native <meter> HTML element, or provide the value information in the accessible name.

bugs.description: VoiceOver on Chrome announces mixed-state checkboxes as 'mixed' instead of 'partially checked'. This differs from VoiceOver on Safari which says 'mixed'.
bugs.workaround: No workaround needed — both convey the mixed state, just with different wording.

bugs.description: When a modal dialog opens, NVDA sometimes does not move focus to the dialog. The user remains focused on the trigger element behind the modal.
bugs.workaround: Explicitly set focus to the first focusable element or the dialog title when the dialog opens. Use aria-modal='true' and manage focus trapping.

bugs.description: JAWS ignores aria-roledescription in Firefox, falling back to the native role name. Works in Chrome and Edge.
bugs.workaround: Test with Chrome/Edge, or don't rely solely on aria-roledescription for critical information.
